lines.en: Several hours later...

Imani and I decide to meet up in the urban district since it’s the closest place (within reasonable distance) that the two of us can go without fear of being caught by some of the other girls I am most likely sleeping with.
She didn’t word it like that. That’s all me. In fact, I’m not sure she even knows that I am sleeping with any of our her students yet. And I doubt she’d like me nearly as much if she did.
But, then again, I thought that with Chika too and we all know how things currently stand on that end.
I think it’s best to probably keep Imani out of it, though. She’s cuter when she lives in whatever world allows her to believe I’m not even half as terrible as I am.
She’s bound to be pulled out of it one day, I’m sure. She’s friends with Osako, after all — and she’s essentially known about Ayane and me for quite some time now without revealing as much to Wakana.
The only question is how long Imani and Wakana (if she’s still oblivious) can remain untainted by my misdeeds. Because I assume the red flags are piling up.
And we’re but one strong gust of wind away from that pile being strewn across their respective living places.
Will they still smile at me even then?
Or will the looks on their faces be one I can not comprehend? Halfway between disappointed and...whatever else a normal person would think about the man (or child) I present myself as.
I suppose that, if all else fails, and my adventurous assistant teacher simply can’t let go of me even when she needs to, I can sever the ties with a knife I’ll call “truth.”
It’s one I only taste the sting of when I can feel nothing else.
And oh, how I wish that were still the case.
: Senpai! Over here!
: Perfect timing! I just got here myself.
: I was worried I was going to be late. I had to wait for a different train since the first one was full of that huge group of Europeans who only show up every now and then.
: The...huge group of who?
: Europeans. Otoha hates them. Anyway, doesn’t matter now. It’s boner time.
: Boner time? But I thought it was Christmas date time.
: Those two things aren’t mutually exclusive. It can be boner date time.
: It’s kind of a bad time for me right now. Biological functions and whatnot.
: That’s okay. You have a mouth.
: Damn, Senpai! You’re really coming out swingin’ today, huh?!
: Sorry. I’ve never been good at “dates” so I normally just try and steer them to the primary objective as soon as I possibly can.
: I didn’t invite you out because I was trying to get laid, Senpai. I like, genuinely just wanted to spend time with you and stuff.
: But if you reeeeeally want me to suck your dick, I guess we can find an alleyway or something. I’m charging you the holiday rate, though.
: No, it’s fine. We can just...genuinely spend time together or whatever.
: For my sake? Nooooooo. It’s clear you’re not going to calm down until somebody sucks your dick. And since nobody else is around, I guess it just haaaas to be me.
: Imani, I’m fine. Really.
: No, no! It’s clear you need this. I insist. But just so you know, I’m doing it for you, not me.
: Pass.

: Question — are you saying “pass” for my sake? Or am I meant to interpret those three consecutive rejections as a sign that you no longer wish to be sexually involved with me despite bringing up boner time?
: Boner time is just my catchphrase at this point. And I do wish to be sexually involved with you. Just not right now since you clearly have other things planned.
: Cool. Because I also wish to continue being sexually involved with you. But I also respect your decision to not put your penis in my mouth right now.
: Rad.
: Even if you totally can if you really want to.
: Again, rad.
: Like, if you were to just go for it, I totally wouldn’t say no.
: How long are you going to keep this up for?
: I don’t know. I am also very bad at dates. Including but not limited to asking people out on them, as I am sure you experienced earlier.
: We have so much in common.
: Right! And you know what else we have in common, Senpai?
: We’ve had at least one sexual encounter with a fruit?
: No, we-
: Wait, what?
: We’re both teachers?
: Hell nah. You’re telling me about this fruit thing.
: Okay. But you have to go first.
: I’ve never done that with a fruit!
: Really? But there are so many phallically shaped ones.
: I know! Which is why I’ve thought about it! But I’ve never actually done it! Now, your turn! Which produce aisle do I need to keep you away from?!
: None. I just wanted to get you to admit something funny.
: You know, it’s good we got this out of the way now. Because if my idea for this date involved introducing you to my parents, I’m not sure they’d appreciate our dialogue.
: They better if you’re flying me all the way to Ghana to meet them.
: Are you thinking what I’m thinking, Senpai?
: Definitely not. I’m still on the fruit thing.
: Well, I’m thinking we should start a comedy duo.
: That would never work, Imani.
: Why not?
: Racism.
: Damn. Foiled again.
: Also, I get stage fright.
: Tch, of course. I knew there had to be a reason you wouldn’t put your penis in my mouth.
: Okay. I’m starting to think we should go somewhere else because I’m worried standing here and bantering like this will lead to us sucking up the rest of the time we have tonight.
: I’m sure there’s some sort of fellatio-related joke to be made there, but now I’m stuck on the fruit thing again too.
: Come. We need to break free from our perpetual state of being hilarious.
: Huh? Oh! Okay. Yeah.
: Do you have somewhere in mind? I don’t really come over here that often. I was okay with doing basically whatever tonight so long as we’re together.
: You’re being way cuter than normal today and I’m going to need you to tone it down before I really do squeeze the life out of you.
: Am I normally not cute? Or is today just a really good day?
: Today is just a really good day, I think.
: It’s probably the hat. Or some kind of Christmas miracle. But the second you start singing, I’m outta here. There are lines that even I must draw, Senpai.
: Senpai?
: I looked up what that thing you said meant.
: Hm?
: I’ve said a lot of things. What are you talking about, exactly?
: The Twi thing. Medɔ wo.
: Eh?! Ah!? Huh?! What!? When?! Why?!
: After that beach trip. It sounded nice, so I wanted to know what it meant.
: Oooooooooh God. Oh no. Forget it. Forget I said that. Forget what it means. Forget everything ever and don’t look at me for at least the next...ten years? Twenty years? Sound good? Good.
: I thought you wanted me to look up what it meant?
: Not like this!
: Is it true, Imani?
: I didn’t think you’d actually look it up! I was just saying things! I do that sometimes!
: So it’s not true then?
: No! Of course not!
: I was just...you know...
: I get...caught up in the mood sometimes and...and words happen.
: But they’re just words, Senpai. You know words. You’re a...writer guy. Surely you can understand, like...context and........stuff.
: So if I told you I love you, you wouldn’t be able to say it back?
: Huh?
: What would you do?
: It’s not nice to mess with girls like this, Senpai. I’m already embarrassed enough.
I thought about saying it.
Really, I did.
There’s just no language I could do it in that she wouldn’t understand.
It took Imani roughly twenty minutes to calm down, and thirty to be able to look me in the eyes again.
I try not to spend too much time thinking about exactly what she meant by those words as, despite not knowing much about love, even I can understand that it has different levels.
And I think in some regard, she really does love me. And in that regard, I probably love her too. But I probably love Wakana as well if we’re going to water down the word like that.
What I don’t understand is when it’s okay to say it. When you’re allowed to love someone. And if I used those words on people like them, what would it mean for girls like Ayane?
I guess it doesn’t matter now. She’s over it, so I should be too.
And I should focus on making this night memorable for her.
I can’t do that if I’m only thinking about myself.
: This is a nice place, Senpai. Festive. And with enough alcohol, I might even be able to forget how insanely embarrassed I am to look you in the eyes again.
: You were able to look me in the eyes without any trouble at all the night I ate you out for several hours straight.
: Because that was less embarrassing. There’s no shame to be had when it comes to sex. Feelings, though? That’s the stuff that gets you.
: I don’t think I’ve ever related to you as much as I do right now, Imani.
: We have so much in common, remember? We both haven’t had sex with any fruit yet.
: “Yet” implies the possibility that it may still happen.
: Let’s hope neither one of us ever reaches that level of loneliness, okay?
: Imani, I have something to confess.
: I knew it! You have! Haven’t you?!
: It was an accident. Probably.
: Yeah, sure. And Timothee Chalamet just tripped and fell into that peach in Call Me By Your Name. I need details. Now.
: I...don’t even know how to provide them. I just know that I have several vague memories of using a watermelon to-
: Wait, a watermelon? Aren’t they a little, like...huge? And hard? And...watery?
: You are asking the wrong person.
: Is...Is there a right person to ask?
: Did...someone make you fuck a watermelon, Senpai?
: You know what? Let’s just talk about Christmas instead. We’ve both embarrassed ourselves enough for tonight.
: I may have practiced sucking dick with a zucchini once.
I knew it.
: Who are we, Imani?
: A couple of weirdos apparently. But it’s that sorta thing that makes us fun, don’t you think?
: Fun is certainly one word for it.
: What- are you not having fun tonight?
: Walking around...making fun of each other...taking in all the lights...the decorations...
: It’s exactly what I wanted out of a Christmas date. And there’s no one I’d rather be here with than you, Senpai.
: I’m really glad you said yes.
: You know, Christmas actually used to be a pretty huge part of my life. Have I ever told you that?
: I don’t think so. But I can feel a flashback coming on, so I’m sure that means you’re going to now.
: Well, I told you my father was a pastor right?
: That sounds familiar, so probably.
: Well, I don’t know how much you know about all that religious mumbo-jumbo, and I’m sure you don’t care either, but my dad looooved Christmas.
: And, as you know, I loved my dad. Which meant that I tried to make him happy any way I could.
: And sometimes, that meant sitting around and listening to him read from the Book of Luke even when all of my brothers and sisters had gotten too old or too bored to bother with that.
: When the angels had left them and gone into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has told us about.”
: So they hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby, who was lying in the manger.
: When they had seen him, they spread the word concerning what had been told them about this child, and all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them.
: But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart.
: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, which were just as they had been told.
: On the eighth day, when it was time to circumcise the child, he was named Jesus, the name the angel had given him before he was conceived.
: Dad, I have a question.
: And I have an answer.
: Why does Jesus have so many names?
: Joshua. Jesus. Yeshua. Son of Man...You’re always referring to him differently. But if he was actually named Jesus-
: They are all his names, Imani.
: The Bible has been adapted more times than one can count. And depending on who is adapting or translating the text, different names are used.
: The name “Yehoshua” or “Yeshua” is mostly used in Hebrew texts. And before we had “Jesus,” we had “Iesus.”
: But it does not matter how his name is spelled, my daughter. What matters is-
: What he stands for and the lessons he can teach us. I know, Dad. I was just confused, that’s all.
: Then how about we take a break for today? You can come with me to the market and help me deliver the banku your mother cooked for-
: I have one more question.
: Of course. What is it?
: What does it mean to “circumcise” a child?
: And that was the first and last time I ever talked to my dad about penises. The end.
: That story took a weird turn near the end.
: It did. But the point is this-
: This holiday, to me, has always been about spending time with the people I care about.
: Not just this year either. The last couple — getting to spend it with you and the girls...it’s been amazing. And I’m truly grateful to have finally found somewhere it feels like I belong.
: But what’s it like for you, Senpai? Do you have anything you always think about when the holidays roll around? Or are you too Japanese for that?
: Christmas is getting pretty popular here, if you haven’t already noticed.
: I have. But what does that mean for you?
: Lately...just Christmas parties.
: Seeing everyone together. Getting roped into both joyous and tragic events one after the other. Letting some people down. Lifting some others up.
: Just another day then?
: Pretty much...yeah.
: I did...mean it, you know.
: That thing I said.
: Like...it might not be love-love yet.
: And...I know you get weird when I talk about this, so I’ll try and keep it brief and...painless, but...
: I’d be really happy if...
: If the rest of my Christmases were just like this one.
: Well, the night’s not over yet.
: I knew you’d come around. But if anybody sees me going down on you, this was your idea, not mine.
: Imani, no. I meant there’s some other sappy, quintessential place the two of us need to go if you really want to call this a Christmas date.
: KFC?
